title: Owner decision needed: is the leaky L2 labeler acceptable evidence for the explanation path?
description:
## Owner decision needed (Q1)

Do not assume an answer. The L2 labeler build waits for it.

1. Is an LLM-simulated labeler that knows a hidden team convention (L2: ≤20 words, never quotes the rule, no comment 40% of the time) acceptable evidence for the explanation path? It **leaks by design**: a gain shows the plumbing works, not that real reviewers' comments surface hidden factors.
2. Labeler model: OpenAI `gpt-6-luna` (same as the analyst; phrasing coupling) or Bedrock Kimi-K3 (already wired in Jev-Flywheel)?
3. Does **any real reviewer feedback with comments** exist? None on disk: every recorded comment is the template "I disagree; the correct label is X" (43 in `fixtures/recordings/simulated-labeler`, about 2,270 in the `bios_attorney` recordings).

## Definition of done

The owner's answers are recorded as a comment here and reflected in the labeler task's scope. Cost: $0.

## Design

[DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md) §2, §7 Q1.

comments.text: Owner decision (2026-10-01): explanations come from a simulated human, an agent consulting its own hidden rubric, as in Jev-Flywheel's recorded simulated-labeler; it supplies feedback with reasons in Phase 2. Real datasets with real reviewer comments come later. The L2 labeler task (decision-flywheel-evaluations-8b8d8513-b626-4f34-87bc-d2b36ffa4312) should follow this; the harness already accepts comments (--comments JSONL of {item_id, comment}) for arms A-c and A-c+F.
